name: Charles de Gaulle
role: French general, leader of Free France, head of the provisional government (1944-46) and President of France (1959-69)
summary: De Gaulle was a nationalist statesman who combined a strong, independent state with an executive above parties. He wrote the Fifth Republic's presidential model, pursued nuclear and diplomatic independence, favoured state-guided growth with worker participation as a 'third way', and ended French Algeria through self-determination.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The provisional government he headed decreed the 1945 social security system, the base of French state-guaranteed health cover.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Historians describe Gaullism as state-guided growth, accepting liberal opinion only where it promises more efficiency than planning; he did not state a general view on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: His provisional government nationalised Renault and founded EDF and Air France, and in late 1945 he outlined further nationalisations and a new economic plan.

cut-welfare.rationale: His government laid the foundations of the French welfare state (social security, 1945); no record of him calling for welfare cuts.

strong-leader.rationale: Argued at Bayeux and in 1958 for a head of state above parties with power to name ministers, call elections and act as arbiter, and for a government 'made to govern'.

state-harmful.rationale: His whole programme rested on a strong state: 'the nation will flourish or perish according to whether the State has enough force'.

empower-police-military.rationale: In 1945-46 he threatened to resign rather than accept a 20 percent cut in the military budget, and as president built the nuclear strike force.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His organising theme was 'a certain idea of France' and national grandeur; Gaullism affirms French heritage and unity.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Rejected supranational bodies: the Fouchet Plan sought an intergovernmental Europe, he caused the 1965 empty chair crisis and withdrew from NATO's integrated command.

nation-first.rationale: Told Johnson France would 'recover the entire exercise of her sovereignty' and leave integrated commands; his foreign policy put national independence first.

state-directs-investment.rationale: As president he backed a planned programme of investment in energy, transport and heavy industry; Gaullism holds the state should give impetus to and guide growth.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bayeux speech describes dictatorship as an adventure ending in ruin and demands institutions that prevent it; he refused the Communists key ministries in 1945.

democracy-best.rationale: Described democracy as expressing opinions through suffrage, and resigned in 1969 when voters rejected his referendum; his institutions were framed as democratic.

direct-votes.rationale: Used referendums repeatedly (1958, 1961, 1962, 1969) and appealed directly to the nation, though also kept parliament.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: he set up parliament plus an elected arbiter president and opposed Communist claims to power; no statement on councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Offered overseas territories in the 1958 Community a vote to accept or break all ties, and accepted Algerian independence; for regions of metropolitan France no such stance, and Quebec remark is a separate case.

political-violence-never.rationale: Called for armed struggle from London and led Free France against Germany and Vichy; the Bayeux speech presents that armed resistance as legitimate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Opposed the Marxist class-conflict view; Gaullism sought capital-labour association to end class struggle.

limit-population.rationale: Bayeux speech set as a national aim to make France 'more numerous' as well as more powerful and fraternal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Historian Berstein calls Gaullism neither doctrine nor ideology but a pragmatic exercise of power; not stated by him in so many words.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: his participation scheme says capital and labour both contribute to an enterprise and both should share its profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bayeux speech condemns dictatorship; in 1945 he refused the Communist party (seen as foreign agent) control of police and armed forces.

organic-representation.rationale: Bayeux speech put representatives of economic, family and intellectual bodies into a second chamber, but kept a first chamber elected by universal suffrage (parties); mixed.

total-state.rationale: Insisted on separated, balanced powers, an independent judiciary as guardian of liberty and warned that dictatorship ends in disaster.

national-rebirth.rationale: Spoke of 'une rénovation profonde' of France at Bayeux and in 1958 said the nation must evolve rapidly or become obsolete.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Bayeux claimed the Saar as naturally linked to France, but he later ended French rule in Algeria; expansion not a stated aim.

single-common-good.rationale: Held that the head of state must reconcile the general interest and that parties express particular interests and national division.

workplace-democracy.rationale: 1968: all workers should be informed and, through freely named representatives, sit on company councils and put forward proposals.

national-self-determination.rationale: Offered Algeria self-determination in 1959, gave Community territories a free vote on leaving, and urged peoples' 'right to dispose of themselves' in Indochina.

class-collaboration.rationale: 1968 TV interview: participation as a 'third solution' giving workers a share of profits and management voice; he wanted men to be partners, not adversaries.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 1958 constitution he presented rejects distinctions of race in legal equality.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: he presented the state as embodying the nation above parties and classes, not as a tool of one class.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His record includes nationalisations, planning, social security and state-led investment.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution he presented guarantees equality of all citizens before the law without distinction of origin, race or religion.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bayeux: public powers are valid only if they rest on the confident adhesion of citizens; building otherwise is 'building on sand'.

separated-powers.rationale: Bayeux and 1958 speeches: legislative, executive and judicial powers should be clearly separated and strongly balanced.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: he accused the Communists of seeking to hijack the Resistance for their own dictatorship and kept them from key ministries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His constitution's Article 16 lets the president take the measures an emergency requires.

party-controls-media.rationale: State monopoly on broadcasting gave government influence over news, yet the written press and elections stayed free.

party-commands-army.rationale: Bayeux gave command of forces to the head of state above parties; in 1958 he ordered officers out of the Committees of Public Safety.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Proposed the intergovernmental Fouchet Plan, called for a Europe of sovereign states, and withdrew French representatives in 1965.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Bayeux: the head of state names ministers, heads the Council and guarantees independence and treaties; the 1958 constitution embodied this.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In his memoirs criticised the Communists for denouncing the war as 'capitalist' after the Molotov-Ribbentrop pact, and he led France's own war effort.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Told Johnson France would remain party to the 1949 treaty and fight beside allies if attacked, but leave integrated commands and recover bases.

people-in-arms.rationale: His 1934 book proposed a mechanised professional elite army of 100,000 men rather than mass armies.

death-penalty.rationale: Supported capital punishment; 35 guillotined and four shot during his presidency, and he refused clemency to OAS plotter Bastien-Thiry.

constituent-assembly.rationale: 1944-46 he had a constituent assembly elected with a referendum on its text; in 1958 his government drafted the constitution with an advisory committee.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Argued from 1954 for a French arsenal, authorised the first test in 1960 and refused the Partial Test Ban Treaty.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Proposed and won the 28 October 1962 referendum making the president directly elected.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He ended a war by leaving Algeria after 132 years of rule, saying it threatened neither honour nor independence.

collective-defense.rationale: Letter to Johnson: France would fight at its allies' side if one were the object of unprovoked aggression.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: In January 1968 he told Ben-Gurion that Israel's seizure of territory amounted to annexation and should be withdrawn from.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Bayeux: head of state 'placed above parties'; 1958: a national arbiter above political struggles.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ended the Algerian war, backed Biafra's breakaway and endorsed Quebec's freedom, though earlier Algerian policy was to keep it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Said his government acted 'in legality' and made the president guarantor of treaties and respect for the constitution.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: His 1958 plan created an independent constitutional committee to judge whether laws are constitutional.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cambodia speech stresses French language and culture there; he sustained influence in former colonies through the Foccart network.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bayeux: head of state elected by a broad college; 1962: direct election by the people.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Declared Vichy's acts null and void and Bayeux says public powers are valid only with citizens' adhesion.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Opposed parliamentary dominance and gave the president arbitration and referendum powers, while parliament still voted laws and budgets.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Quoted Solon at Bayeux: the best constitution depends on which people and which epoch.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Ordered officers to quit the Committees of Public Safety and 'neutralised' the army in Algeria in 1958.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Bayeux: final vote on laws and budgets belongs to an Assembly elected by direct universal suffrage.

non-intervention.rationale: Condemned US intervention in Vietnam, but armed Biafra and endorsed Quebec's freedom.

defeat-communism.rationale: Pursued détente: recognised China, spoke of Europe from Atlantic to Urals, and said Vietnam needs a political solution.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: denounced dictatorship and the longing for liberty it provokes, and kept free elections and press.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Promoted worker participation in firms and opposed leaving all decisions to remote bodies.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Gaullism claims to transcend left and right; he put himself above parties.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: 1958: the Republic is the sovereignty of the people; Bayeux grounds authority in citizens.

social-market-economy.rationale: Gaullist third way: market economy with participation and social protection under state guidance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built armed forces and a nuclear strike force and refused unilateral disarmament.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Left NATO's integrated command and sought to avoid a bipolar world but stayed in the Alliance.

property-franchise.rationale: Granted votes to women, introduced direct presidential election and a constitution declaring suffrage universal and equal.

racial-franchise.rationale: Presented a constitution with universal suffrage and equality of citizens without distinction of race; referendum open to all in overseas territories.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Bayeux: the state must preserve public order and see justice done.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Wanted to end the permanent presence of allied military elements on French soil and ordered foreign personnel out.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Described France as a person with whom a mystical dialogue ran throughout history.

second-chamber.rationale: Bayeux: a second chamber elected differently to examine and amend.

sacred-nation.rationale: Presented France as a mystical person with historic destiny.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Built a French arsenal and kept it while refusing disarmament.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Free French authority he led granted women the vote on 21 April 1944, confirmed by his provisional government.

indirect-election.rationale: Switched from an electoral college to direct popular election of the president in 1962.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Appealed directly to the nation through referendums over parties.

multipolar-world.rationale: Sought a world not dominated by two superpowers and recognised China; Europe as a third pole.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Combined national greatness with participation of workers.

notes: Changed views: Algeria (integration rhetoric in 1958, self-determination from September 1959). Mixed evidence on constitutional assemblies (1946 vs 1958). Some answers rely on Wikipedia summaries.
